rounds.response:
Audience & Segmentation: Start from explicit, recorded promotional consent per the Compliance "Product Promotional Consent" standard; Primary Cohort = contacts with that consent + strong willingness-to-pay signals (recent premium trial within 6 months, top-tier spend in the last 12 months, or ICP-matched usage) + recent engagement (opened/clicked in last 12 months); Secondary Cohort = contacts with that consent + general engagement in the last 12 months but without high-value signals; Exclusions = unsubscribed/hard-bounce/complaint flags, jurisdictional opt-outs, and internal do-not-email lists.  
Cadence & Frequency: Recommended default—Primary Cohort: up to 3 promotional touches/week for the first six weeks post-launch (blended: personalized promotion, value/feature messaging, and clear pricing/CTA); Secondary Cohort: 1 value-focused promotional touch/week with explicit invitation to opt into higher-frequency communications.  
Hard controls and data use: Enforce per-contact caps (absolute max 4 promotional touches/week across Acme email channels and no more than 1 send/day), require that personalization only uses signals authorized in the Compliance doc, and apply exclusion lists and suppression logic before segmentation.  
Monitoring and rollback: Monitor deliverability, complaint and unsubscribe rates against Compliance-defined thresholds (to be confirmed in the working session); automated throttling and immediate cadence reduction will trigger if thresholds breach, and Sales will be notified of account-level complaint spikes.  
Rationale/positioning: This unified recommendation honors Compliance’s consent-first rule and Sales’ quality filters while preserving Marketing’s growth levers via a consented, two-tiered audience (Marketing’s broader 12‑month engaged pool appears as the Secondary Cohort and as an alternative in Key Decisions & Trade-offs rather than the default).

Audience & Segmentation: Baseline is consent-first—every contact must have explicit, recorded product-category promotional consent per Compliance; Primary Cohort = consented contacts with strong willingness‑to‑pay signals (recent premium trial within 6 months, top-tier spend in last 12 months, or ICP‑matched usage) AND recent engagement (opened/clicked in last 12 months); Secondary Cohort = consented contacts with engagement in the last 12 months but without the high-value signals; Exclusions = unsubscribed/hard-bounce/complaint flags, jurisdictional opt-outs, and internal DNE lists.

Key Decisions & Trade‑offs – Audience & Cadence: (1) Baseline = consent-first, two-tier (Primary = consent + value signals, 3/wk) to balance growth and risk; (2) Marketing aggressive variant = treat all consented 12‑month engaged as primary with up to 4/wk and broader behavioral personalization (higher upside, higher compliance/complaint risk); (3) Compliance concern = strict consent precondition and adherence to historical complaint/unsubscribe thresholds; (4) Sales concern = protect lead quality via Primary cohort definition and track early churn/no-shows and rep feedback so cadence can be adjusted.
